Cobalt

Cobalt (Co), atomic number 27. This element-level record uses the ChEBI cobalt-atom identifier for chemical identity. Cobalt-bearing cathodes and mixed battery black mass are material forms and secondary resources, respectively; neither is a mineral species or synonymous with the element. The dated US designation maps the listed cobalt commodity to this element record; it does not designate every cobalt-bearing mineral or waste stream.

	Element	Critical
European Union Regulation (EU) 2024/1252, Annex II, Section 1, List of critical raw materials (critical); United States of America USGS Final List of Critical Minerals (critical)
	1
Bioleaching
	—	
CHEBI:27638

Chalcopyrite

Chalcopyrite is the mineral species with IMA-approved formula CuFeS2. The September 2026 IMA list records status G (grandfathered) and the uncertain original-description year 1725 ?. That year is not an IMA approval number. This mineral species is distinct from elemental copper, the copper commodity, and an impure flotation concentrate. The curated bioleaching experiment concerns an Aitik concentrate; its copper-element representation in cmmmech:copper is the same experiment, not an independent replication. No constituent-element criticality is inherited.

	Mineral	—	1
Bioleaching
	
Acidithiobacillus caldus
Sulfobacillus thermosulfidooxidans
Leptospirillum ferriphilum
	—

Asbolane

Asbolane is a hydrous manganese oxide mineral with variable associated hydroxide cations, listed as grandfathered with historical year 1841 in the September 2026 IMA-CNMNC list. Its listed formula is Mn4+(O,OH)2·(Co,Ni,Mg,Ca)x(OH)2x·nH2O. It is distinct from elemental manganese, cobalt and nickel, from lateritic ore, and from an arbitrary cobalt-doped birnessite preparation. The experiment below uses a synthetic Co/Ni-bearing powder that the source assigns to asbolane by XRD; no independent refinement establishes ideal composition or complete phase purity. No commodity criticality is inherited.

	Mineral	—	1
Redox Transformation
	
Geobacter sulfurreducens
	—

Birnessite

Birnessite is a layered manganese oxide mineral, listed as grandfathered in the September 2026 IMA-CNMNC list with formula (Na,Ca,K)0.6(Mn4+,Mn3+)2O4(H2O)1.5. Its composition and polytype vary. It is distinct from elemental manganese, mixed manganese ore and nodules, the buserite precursor used to prepare some synthetic analogues, and manganese oxalate products. The mechanisms below concern separately prepared synthetic sodium and cobalt-bearing forms, and a source-assigned poorly crystalline biogenic Mn-oxide/fungal composite. They do not establish behavior for natural ore or every birnessite polytype. No criticality designation is inherited from manganese.

	Mineral	—	4

Paraconiothyrium sp. WL-2

Carrollite

Carrollite is the CuCo2S4 mineral species, listed as grandfathered with original-description year 1852 in the September 2026 IMA list. It is distinct from elemental cobalt or copper, dissolved metal ions, mixed cobalt-bearing ores and mine tailings. The evidence below concerns laboratory surface alteration of source-identified natural carrollite crystals in an acidophile culture system. It does not establish an isolated-metal recovery yield or industrial deployment. No criticality designation is inherited from constituent elements.

Antimony (Sb), represented as an element distinct from antimonate feed, sorbed antimonite and sulfide-bearing products. A sediment-inoculated laboratory experiment supports transformation through coupled microbial and chemical reactions under sulfidogenic conditions. The United States 2025 critical-mineral designation names the antimony commodity; it does not designate every Sb compound, host mineral or secondary resource.
